work_order.understanding:
Issue #46 carries four non-blocking findings from the review of #45. I re-checked all four against the code as it stands after #45 merged (1fa7d9a); all four still reproduce, and none was closed by a later commit.

1. test/web/pages.test.js:127 asserts `/<h1 class="page-title" data-testid="page-title">[^<]*<\/h1>/`. It pins the CSS class and the attribute order, so a purely cosmetic rename of `.page-title` in src/web/styles.css:137 fails 25 route x state assertions. This contradicts .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md, which says class names are styling hooks, not assertions. The same test already gets this right on the next line (`/<h1[^>]*>([^<]*)<\/h1>/` for the text).

2. docs/ui.md:23 says "one display size for KPI values, one body size, one caption size", but .page-title (styles.css:140) is now also 1.4rem, the same value as .kpi-value (styles.css:195), so the display step has a second user the spec does not mention. The five **Regions** lines in docs/ui.md (59, 73, 87, 101 and the fifth screen) do not list the page title that layout() now emits as the first region inside main. The drift is real, but docs/ui.md is an approved doc no ticket may change, so it is recorded in risks for a human and is not in files[].

3. src/web/styles.css:139 `.page-title { color: var(--color-ink) }` is a no-op. I enumerated every `color:` declaration in the stylesheet: body (32), a (39), .app-header .brand (72), .app-header nav a (83), .app-header nav a[aria-current] (92), .page-footer (116), .page-title (139), .banner-warn (168), .kpi-label (188), .check-time (232), .maturity-label (257), .button (303), .button-secondary (310). Every one except 139 overrides an inherited or UA value. The h1's parent is main#main (pages.js:75-78) and #main (styles.css:107-113) declares max-width, margin, padding, display and gap but no color, so the h1 already inherits --color-ink from body.

4. test/web/pages.test.js:123 uses Array.prototype.reduce purely for its side effect, asserting inside the callback. `grep -rn "\.reduce(" test/` returns four hits; the other three (test/data/append-only.test.js:74, test/domain/money.test.js:43 and :51) use reduce to compute a sum. The same file iterates with `for (const ... of ...)` at lines 49, 112, 113, 174, 218, 262, 322, 493, 497, 605.
work_order.root_cause: The #45 work order asked only for "the h1 carries data-testid=\"page-title\"" and left the styling class in the same assertion, so a rendering concern (the class) was bound into a behavioural check. The two stylesheet and test-style findings are ordinary leftovers of a change that was correct but not swept afterwards: a restated inherited colour, and a reduce used for its side effect because the assertion was written as one expression. None is a defect in behaviour -- all 25 route x state shells render correctly today.
work_order.approach:
Three surgical edits, no behaviour change, no new dependency, no new abstraction.

(1) Extract the h1 hook matcher in test/web/pages.test.js to a module-level constant and make it class-free: `const H1_HOOK = /<h1[^>]*\bdata-testid="page-title"[^>]*>[^<]*<\/h1>/;`, then assert `assert.match(html, H1_HOOK, ...)` in place of the inline regex. `[^>]*` on both sides of the testid means the attribute may appear in any position and the class may be present, renamed, or absent, while a missing h1, a missing testid, or an h1 with nested markup inside it still fails. Add a new test in the same file that exercises H1_HOOK directly against four literal strings, so the relaxation cannot silently become vacuous.

(2) Delete `color: var(--color-ink);` from the `.page-title` rule in src/web/styles.css. Leave the margin, font-size and line-height declarations and the existing explanatory comment untouched -- the comment is still accurate about the display size.

(3) Rewrite the heading-order check in test/web/pages.test.js as the for...of the rest of the suite uses, keeping the seed of 0, the same comparison and the same failure message, and updating the comment above it, which currently says "Reduce from 0".

I verified there is no third caller to worry about: `grep -rn "page-title" src/ test/ docs/` returns exactly three hits (pages.js:56 emits it, styles.css:137 styles it, pages.test.js:127 asserts on it), so relaxing the assertion touches nothing else.

Do not add a replacement declaration or a comment about the deletion; the rule is about size and spacing, and colour is inherited from body.

risks: Finding 2 (docs/ui.md) is NOT fixed here and this PR will not fully close issue #46. docs/ui.md:23 states "one display size for KPI values, one body size, one caption size", but .page-title is now also 1.4rem (styles.css:140), the same value as .kpi-value (styles.css:195) -- the display step has a second user the spec does not mention. Separately, none of the five **Regions** lines in docs/ui.md (lines 59, 73, 87, 101, and the fifth screen section) mentions the page title, which layout() (src/web/pages.js:75-78) now emits as the first region inside main on all 25 shells. docs/ui.md is an approved doc that no ticket may change, so this needs a human edit.

Relaxing the h1 assertion weakens it slightly in one direction: it no longer proves the h1 is the .page-title element. That is deliberate -- the class is a styling hook per .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md -- and the new matcher cases plus the existing h1-count, hierarchy and text assertions cover what the class-coupled version was actually protecting. If a future design genuinely needs a different h1 to carry the hook, that is a new requirement, not a regression.

The `[^<]*` in H1_HOOK still rejects an h1 whose content contains nested markup, so it is not as permissive as a bare `/<h1[^>]*data-testid="page-title"/`. That is intentional: it keeps the assertion meaningful about a non-empty text heading. Do not loosen it to the bare form.

No path in this change touches forbidden_paths in .sdlc/config.yml. The change deletes no data, touches no money, policy-kernel or executor path, and adds no network host, so env.api_allowlist is unaffected.

triage.diagnosis: The qa stage did not fail on the code, the plan, or the environment — it failed on the shape of the path strings in its own report, and the browser work it had already paid for is sitting in an artifact. QA finished successfully (the agent returned is_error:false after 60 turns / 6m18s / $3.01) and wrote a schema-valid qa-report.json: verdict pass, 0 bugs, 12 tests, all four ACs rolled up. The judge job's `validate` step printed `valid`. The very next step, .sdlc/bin/check-evidence.mjs, died for two reasons, both about citation formatting and neither about evidence. (1) Every one of the 15 slash-bearing citations was written relative to $QA_EVIDENCE_DIR (shells/root-ideal.png, a11y/narrow-root.png, video/error-retry.mp4, edge/-state-fancy.png, ...) rather than from the repository root. check-evidence.mjs:63 does `resolve(p)`, which resolves a relative path against cwd (the repo root), so `shells/root-ideal.png` becomes <repo>/shells/root-ideal.png, `relative(dir, abs)` yields `../shells/...` and :64 marks it lost. All 15 files actually exist at exactly those paths inside qa-evidence/ in the uploaded artifact — nothing was lost to /tmp; the check simply could not see them. (2) T-3 and T-4 were reported as proving a passing criterion while 'citing no evidence file', but each of them cites three real files (mutations.log, mutations.json, node-test-output.txt / exchange-opportunities-partial.txt). They were not counted because :48 defines `local = (e) => /[/\]/.test(e) && !/^https?:/.test(e)` — a path separator as a proxy for 'is a local file' — and :76 reuses that predicate to decide whether a test cites evidence at all. A top-level file in the evidence dir has no separator, so `mutations.log` reads as no evidence even though it is a 2,320-byte file sitting in the uploaded artifact. I downloaded the artifact (qa-evidence, run 36170701585, 9.5 MB, not expired) and reproduced the failure byte-for-byte: files=94, predates=, and the identical two complaints. Prefixing the citations with `qa-evidence/` and changing nothing else — same 94 files, same 12 tests, same verdict — makes the real gate print `evidence: 94 file(s) collected, 48 cited, all present` and exit 0, with the PNG magic, HAR parse and HAR 5xx checks all passing. So the evidence is real, the pass is real, and the report is a formatting miss away from standing. Nothing here is transient, nothing is wrong with PR #50 or the work order, and a re-run would drive the browser again for the same screenshots.

Verified by re-running the gate on the downloaded artifact: unmodified report reproduces the failure exactly; the same report with `qa-evidence/` prefixed to every evidence path exits 0 with `94 file(s) collected, 48 cited, all present`. All 15 'lost' paths confirmed present under qa-evidence/ in the artifact, as are mutations.log, mutations.json and node-test-output.txt (94 files total, matching files=94).

framework_defect.what: Its fatal `die()` at line 136 runs in the judge job before post-qa-report, so a report rejected by the evidence check is never recorded on the ledger and can never be handed back. The judge job died here at :2115; the next step was dispatch-fix, and state/46.json has no `rejected_artifacts` key at all. resolve-deployment.mjs:17-27 (handBackRejected) only reads ledger.rejected_artifacts['qa-report'], which the validate step populates — and validate passed here. So the next qa attempt will find no previous-output.json and will start blind, with nothing telling it that citation format is what sank the last one. This is the same failure mode the file's own comment at lines 32-42 records as already fixed once, for the unparseable-report case, where the fix was to stop being fatal and let the next step name the problem. That fix was applied to the parse path only; the evidence path still dies fatally. A secondary defect in the same file: line 48's `local()` requires a path separator, and line 76 reuses it to decide whether a test cites evidence, so a real top-level file like `mutations.log` is reported as no evidence at all — which is how T-3 and T-4 were falsely described in this run's own failure message.
framework_defect.fix: Two changes, both in this file. (1) Stop the evidence check from killing the judge job: on the `pass` path, emit the complaints as `::error::` annotations and `setOutput('problems', ...)`, then exit 0, so the job continues to post-qa-report, which records the rejection on the ledger exactly as validate does — the same treatment the unparseable-report path already got at lines 33-42. Leave the `die()` for the `!kept` case at line 161, where no evidence was collected at all and there is genuinely nothing to keep. (2) Replace the bare-filename blind spot by resolving a citation against `dir` when it is not absolute and does not already sit under it — i.e. try `resolve(dir, p)` as well as `resolve(p)` before declaring it lost — and define the 'cites no evidence' predicate as 'has a non-http entry that resolves to a file under dir', rather than reusing `local()`'s separator test. Add a case for a top-level evidence file (e.g. `mutations.log`) and one for a path relative to the evidence dir, so the two citation forms are both covered and neither silently accepted nor falsely rejected.
